key_insight: PATS turns rollout experiences into a dynamic training scaffold, giving weak agent policies just enough adaptive guidance to learn better long-horizon behavior while gradually removing redundant help as the policy improves.
engineering_relevance: This is useful for building more sample-efficient and token-efficient agent training pipelines, especially when environment rewards are sparse and naive exploration repeatedly fails.
method: Convert rollout groups from the latest policy into evidence cards.
Use task-specific evaluation to revise the prompt/context for subsequent rollouts, adding concrete guidance when needed.
Optimize the policy with standard RLVR, then discard the scaffold at deployment.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports up to 18.6% improvement on ALFWorld and WebShop, and competitive results on seven search-augmented QA benchmarks with 32.1% fewer prompt tokens than the baseline.
watch_item: Because the scaffold is task-specific and dynamically updated, implementation quality may depend heavily on evaluation design and prompt-management overhead.
paper_title: PATS: Policy-Aware Training Scaffolding for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
